articles.title_orig: Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, November 10, 2026
articles.title_zh: Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, November 10, 2026
articles.source: Institute for the Study of War
articles.content_orig:
Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment
The Kremlin is attempting to center the ongoing US-Russia-Ukraine trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi around significant changes to the European security architecture — an effort to revive its 2021 ultimatums to the United States and NATO about rolling back NATO’s presence in Europe. Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov claimed on November 10 that it is “absolutely reasonable” to first negotiate the future of the European security architecture and only then move to resolving the war in Ukraine.[1] An unspecified source in the Russian delegation in Abu Dhabi similarly claimed on November 10 that the settlement of the war in Ukraine is “only one point” in a larger discussion on security architecture and is “subordinated” to the main goal of reshaping Europe’s “comprehensive” and “indivisible” security architecture.[2] Russian statements about the European security architecture refer to Russia’s December 2021 demands that NATO halt new weapons and military personnel deployments to NATO states that joined the alliance after 1997, essentially giving Russia a veto on NATO policy and restricting states’ sovereign choices to join NATO.[3] The Kremlin recently renewed its original 2021 demands of NATO, contradicting Former Senior Advisor to the US President Jared Kushner’s statements in recent days that each country must retain its sovereignty and authority over its security and alliances following peace negotiations to end the war in Ukraine and that NATO will remain central to European collective defense.[4]
The Kremlin has repeatedly tried to justify its war against Ukraine by falsely claiming that the possibility of NATO expansion to include Ukraine threatened Russian security. The Kremlin has long alleged that NATO expansion was one of the “root causes” of the war that peace talks must resolve.[5] Neither NATO nor Ukraine, in fact, took any meaningful action towards bringing Ukraine into NATO between 2008 and 2022, however.[6] NATO has never presented a threat to Russian security, but Putin invaded Ukraine in 2022 to break NATO and Western unity, as ISW has long assessed.[7] The Kremlin’s long-running cognitive warfare campaign falsely blaming NATO and Ukraine for threatening Russian sovereignty aims to justify Russian efforts to reassert control over former Soviet states and does not reflect a genuine Russian concern for its security.
US, Ukrainian, and European officials publicly agreed on the need for credible post-war security guarantees for Ukraine and the involvement of European officials in future multilateral negotiations to end the war in Ukraine — conditions that the Kremlin has repeatedly and explicitly rejected. US, Ukrainian, and European officials held trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi wherein they agreed on the need for credible security guarantees for Ukraine and the involvement of European officials in future multilateral negotiations to end the war.[8] US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, US Special Envoy to the Middle East Steve Witkoff, and Kushner emphasized on November 9 and 10 that a lasting settlement to the war requires durable post-war security guarantees for Ukraine, future involvement of European officials in peace negotiations, and direct engagement between Russia and European officials on broader geopolitical security arrangements.[9] Several Western media outlets reported on November 9 and 10 that US officials asked the Kremlin if it would accept NATO-style Article 4 and Article 5 security guarantees for Ukraine from the United States and NATO that would allow Ukraine to request consultations with NATO states when Ukraine’s territorial integrity is under threat and to receive assistance from the alliance in the event of a future attack.[10]
Russian officials have repeatedly rejected the idea of Western security guarantees for Ukraine since 2025 and the possibility of European officials having a seat at the negotiating table so long as the European position falls short of fully embracing Russia’s maximalist demands.[11] Lavrov claimed on November 10 that US meetings with European representatives in Abu Dhabi are not a “promising approach” to negotiations.[12] Russian State Duma Deputy Alexander Asafov stated on November 10 that Russia’s expectations for the Abu Dhabi talks are “quite modest” and claimed that European participation in the talks could “paralyze” negotiations before they even begin.[13] These statements are consistent with Moscow’s explicit rejections in previous weeks of European participation in negotiations to end the war in Ukraine and go against US, Ukrainian, and European statements in favor of including European officials in future peace talks.[14]
Reported proposals to redraw the administrative borders of Donetsk and Luhansk oblasts to allow Russia to claim that it seized all of the Donbas region and compel Russia to accept a deal to end the war neglect Moscow’s wider territorial aims in Ukraine that go far beyond these two oblasts. The Economist reported on November 9 that US negotiators recently proposed that Ukraine change the administrative borders of Donetsk and Luhansk oblasts as part of a territorial agreement between Russia and Ukraine such that Russia could claim full control of the two regions without Ukraine surrendering the remaining territory of Donbas that it currently holds.[15] The reported proposal suggests that the new oblast borders would correspond to the territory in Donetsk and Luhansk oblasts that Russian forces have seized, although it is unclear what legal status the Ukrainian-controlled territory in Donetsk and Luhansk oblasts would have. Russian President Vladimir Putin has demonstrated, however, that his territorial ambitions in Ukraine go far beyond Donbas.[16] Russia illegally annexed Luhansk, Donetsk, Kherson, and Zaporizhia oblasts in September 2022, and the Kremlin has long conditioned Russian society to expect Russia’s illegal annexation of these parts of Ukraine to be permanent.[17] Russian officials also regularly claim that “Novorossiya” — an amorphous invented region in southern and eastern Ukraine — is an integral part of Russia.[18] Novorossiya notably includes not only occupied Crimea and the four oblasts that Russia has illegally annexed, but also the Kharkiv, Dnipropetrovsk, Mykolaiv, and Odesa oblasts.[19]
Putin and the Russian military command have created a false reality based on exaggerated claims of sweeping advances across the frontline such that the Kremlin would likely try to exploit any discussion of redrawing administrative borders based on the frontline to serve Russia’s interest. Senior Russian military and political officials regularly make blatantly false claims of Russian advances on the frontline, often as far as tens of kilometers from the observed frontline.[20] Putin notably claimed on September 2 that Russian forces had seized Svyatohirsk (14 kilometers northwest of Lyman), despite Ukrainian counterattacks having pushed the frontline over 20 kilometers east of the settlement.[21] A leaked Russian Ministry of Defense (MoD) map from April 2026 also demonstrated that the Russian military command has a severely distorted view of the frontline, with claims of Russian advances in western Zaporizhia Oblast far beyond even the furthest claims from Russian milbloggers at that time.[22] The Russian MoD has also made several false claims in recent months about the encirclement of Ukrainian forces in northern Kharkiv Oblast and Dobropillya, Donetsk Oblast, despite providing no evidence to support the claims.[23] These exaggerations are a part of a broader cognitive warfare effort that aims to convince the West to force Ukraine to capitulate to Russia’s demands.[24] Such a vast disconnect between the true battlefield realities and Russian official claims about the frontline would complicate any attempt to redraw the administrative boundaries of Donetsk and Luhansk oblasts and would risk Moscow claiming it holds more territor

articles.title_orig: US, China to cooperate on AI risks but differences remain: US Treasury Secretary
articles.title_zh: US, China to cooperate on AI risks but differences remain: US Treasury Secretary
articles.content_orig:
The U.S. and China should "harbor no illusions" about their differences as they engage to contain the risks of artificial intelligence, while competing with each other at the same time, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said.
Bessent said in prepared remarks to the National Committee on U.S.-China Relations in New York Tuesday that the two governments had established a new dialogue mechanism on "super intelligence," or SI, aimed at guarding against "shared risks" and averting any "misunderstanding between our two systems."
The mechanism will see both sides exchanging "best practices" for testing advanced models before they are released, and "keeping human judgement firmly in command of the technology," Bessent said, expecting both sides to alert each other to serious incidents involving the SI models.
Bessent, however, stopped short of making any commitment to limit advancement of the technology, as Beijing and Washington remain locked in an intense race to achieve global dominance in AI.
The Trump administration has largely resisted broadening restrictions on AI development over concerns of ceding a competitive edge to China, though the president has more recently signaled some openness to putting in place regulatory safeguards.
"I ​don't mind guardrails," he said in a CBS interview released Sunday , adding that ⁠he did not want regulations to put the U.S. in "a deep second position" behind China, ​which he ​said ⁠had no such restrictions.
China's foreign ministry in September dismissed calls to slow down frontier models, saying that fearmongering and confrontation would only disrupt global AI governance. Huiyao Wang, founder of Center for China and Globalization, a think tank that closely aligns with Beijing's thinking, said last month that the U.S.-China talks should "confront AI risks and manage them together."
During Xi's September visit, Washington and Beijing agreed to launch an AI dialogue with a communications channel to help defuse serious incidents. The two leaders are expected to meet for the third time next week, with Bessent joining, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Leaders' Meeting from Nov. 18 to 19.
As the technology advances, the two nations will need to demonstrate how they can "reconcile the demands of competition with the responsibilities of leadership," Bessent said in his Tuesday speech. "Our interests will not always coincide, and our approach to every challenge likewise will not always converge," he added.
Washington had briefly suspended access by foreign nationals to Anthropic's Mythos and Fable 5 models in June before restoring it weeks later . The U.S. government has also restricted exports of the most advanced chips to Beijing, and accused Chinese developers of copying American models through what it calls industrial-scale distillation.
Xie Feng, China's ambassador to the U.S., told the audience at the gala that efforts by both countries were "indispensable" to addressing issues from global flashpoints to "improving artificial intelligence governance." Cooperation "may not resolve every challenge," he said, but "none can be resolved without it."
The event was organized at a time when controversy around Nvidia Corp CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy has been making headlines.
The billionaire tech executive, who joined Trump's delegation to Beijing in May and was invited to the state dinner in Washington in September, is at the center of a major corporate and national security scandal after admitting to an extramarital affair with a Chinese businesswoman whom the U.S. intelligence officials suspect of espionage.
While Huang's presence at the upcoming summit has been thrown into doubt, other business leaders such as Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk and Mastercard's Michael Miebach could be on Trump's delegation next week, according to South China Morning Post .

articles.title_orig: Israel’s newly elected parliament is already moving against Netanyahu
articles.title_zh: Israel’s newly elected parliament is already moving against Netanyahu
articles.content_orig:
In the last few days, in marked contrast to an election campaign defined by its bitterness and the closeness of its personal attacks, Israel’s current prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu has spoken of national unity and coming together with the opposition bloc that edged out his ruling coalition in October’s election.
On Saturday, the same day that Israeli President Isaac Herzog tasked former Chief of Staff Gadi Eisenkot with forming a government capable of commanding the Knesset, Netanyahu published a video on his social media account claiming Israel to be facing the genuine risk of civil war i f a government were established with the support of Arab parties which he accused of wanting to “eliminate the State of Israel”.
Two days later, Netanyahu returned to the theme of existential threat in a further video, calling upon the leaders of the more successful bloc to recognise the “needs of the hour” and join, under his leadership, a single unified government that would also include the ultra-Orthodox parties, at least one of which is understood to be in talks with Eisenkot, as well as the prime minister’s controversial allies on the far right, Bezalel Smotrich and Itamar Ben-Gvir.
“It’s all a game at the moment. It’s leverage, it’s one-upmanship, it’s psyops, it’s spin, it’s counter-spin,” former Israeli government adviser Daniel Levy said of the invariably long and complex negotiations that take place ahead of establishing a government,
Currently, with the new Knesset being sworn in on Tuesday, speculation is focussing on the role of the Ultra Orthodox, or haredim, parties, which have traditionally offered support to Netanyahu in return for measures shielding their young male yeshiva students from the military draft in defiance off a Super Court ruling of June 2024 .
Nevertheless, irrespective of the past political cover offered to their members by Netanyahu, there are suggestions that one of the Ultra Orthodox parties United Torah Judaism (UTJ) – which refused to endorse Netanyahu’s selection to build a government by the President – is preparing to throw in behind Eisenkot, with the objections of one of the opposition’s principal figures Avigdor Lieberman said to be quieted in the face of either partnering with one of the Arab parties or the continued rule of Lieberman’s nemesis, Netanyahu and the prospect of further elections.
“‘It’s political strategy, that’s all,” Netanyahu’s former aide, Israeli pollster Mitchell Barak said from Jerusalem. ‘But he’s negotiating from a weakened position. With the UTJ, Eisenkot’s got 67 seats,’ he said of the numbers needed to gain a working majority in the 120 seat Knesset, “so, of course, Netanyahu’s going to do all he can to reinforce his bloc; Barak said of negotiations regarded by many as critical to Netanyahu’s personal future.
Netanyahu faces a number of challenges that speak directly to both his political legacy and personal freedom that he will lose all influence over should Eisenkot succeed him.
Foremost are like to be the multiple corruption charges that is is presently on trial for and, despite his claims of innocence that he has already preemptively petitioned the country’s President and his former political rival, Isaac Herzog for. Secondly, and more pressingly is the question of his and his government’s culpability for the alleged failings ahead of the October 7 Hamas led attack that triggered the genocide unleashed upon Gaza by Israel and the multiple strikes and attacks launched by Israel non regional neighbors in the years since.
Many of the new MKs being sworn in on Tuesday, including bereaved family members, reservists, advocates for the 250 or so Israelis taken captive that day and Eisenkot himself, who lost a son and two nephews in the genocide that followed, are all tied directly to October 7 and the wars that followed together creating a chamber where feelings over the October 7 attack and where culpability for its lies are said to run close to the surface.
In particular, attention is likely to focus sharply on Netanyahu himself, whose supposed miscalculations ahead of the attack, stories of numerous missed warnings and who was subsequently accused of dragging out the war, or sacrificing the welfare off the captives for his own political ends. Key among the opposition’s aims for the first day of parliamentary business is set to be the installation of Matan Kahana, a member of Eisenkot’s Yashar (“straight”) party and a keen advocate of a state inquiry into Netanyahu and the government’s failings ahead of the Hamas led attack.
“Having so many people connected so directly to October 7 is going to increase the temperature, but it’s become so politicized that a win for one side automatically becomes a loss for the other, so the bereaved family on the right can say we need to increase our militarism in honor of my son, and the bereaved family in the center says we need to enlist more people.
“Netanyahu can try to influence that but for the first time in a long time, he seems a bit lost,” Israeli political analyst Nimrod Flaschenberg said.
However, how lost Netanyahu may be, or how grounded his claims of pending civil war or destruction at the hands of regional adversaries may be, ultimately, his political and potentially personal fate now lies with an opposition that outstrips his own numerically and a volatile Knesset eager to comb over the mistakes of the past.
“There’s no appetite on the other side to go in with Netanyahu for a unity government,” Levy said,
“The only real circumstances under which that happen is if he can create a security emergency,” he said following a weekend where the UK press had reported daily phone calls from Netanyahu to the Trump administration urging renewed war on Iran.

articles.title_orig: China's car sales seen falling below 19 million units for first time since 2014
articles.title_zh: China's car sales seen falling below 19 million units for first time since 2014
articles.content_orig:
Americans may finally find some relief at the pump.
The national average price of regular gasoline fell below $4 a gallon for the first time since July, reaching $3.9788 on Tuesday, according to AAA . Prices are down about 17 cents from a week ago and nearly 39 cents from a month ago.
The decline comes after energy inflation slowed significantly in October. Energy prices increased 0.7% during the month, a far cry from the 5.2% surge seen in September, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics . The BLS' gasoline index increased 1% over the month, after advancing 9.1% in September.
Bespoke Investment Group pointed out that gasoline prices also tend to decline at this time of the year, making part of the recent relief seasonal.
"While lower oil prices have been a tailwind for the relief at the pump, it's also perfectly normal for gas prices to be falling at this time of year, so if they weren't, there would really be something wrong," the firm said.
The drop at the pump followed a sharp retreat in crude oil. International oil benchmark Brent crude on Tuesday briefly fell below $90 a barrel for the first time since August as comments from U.S. President Donald Trump fueled hopes for an end to Washington's nearly nine-month conflict with Iran.
Recovering oil flows from the Persian Gulf have also eased supply concerns. Regional crude exports have returned to an estimated 80% to 85% of prewar levels, including pipeline shipments, according to ING .
"Energy markets remain under pressure as hopes for a de-escalation in the Middle East reduce geopolitical risk premiums. Oil extended its losses as Gulf supply flows continued to recover, while European gas also moved lower," analysts at ING wrote.
However, the Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller warned Tuesday that energy shocks may have more persistent effects on inflation than they did before the pandemic.
"While I am pleased to see energy prices down from their high rates over the past week or so, they are still quite elevated relative to the start of the year, and the ultimate effect on inflation will depend on what levels are sustained," he said.

articles.title_zh: Anthropic IPO valuation calculator: How much is it really worth?
articles.content_orig:
Anthropic said it will offer 825 million shares in its upcoming IPO at a price range between $70 and $78 per share, according to an updated filing on Tuesday, bringing the 5-year-old artificial intelligence lab a step closer to a potentially historic Nasdaq debut.
The company is planning to price on Nov. 18 and trade on Nov. 19, according to people familiar with the details who were granted anonymity because they were not authorized to speak publicly. Anthropic is targeting retail allocation of about 20%, the people said, a much higher percentage than the typical initial public offering, which is 5% to 10% for retail investors.
At the high end of the range, Anthropic would net up to $64.35 billion in proceeds through the IPO. The company could end up being worth up to $1.405 trillion on a fully diluted basis, rising from the $965 billion valuation it announced as part of a funding round in May.
Anthropic said it has entered into an agreement with Advanced Micro Devices , Broadcom , Google , Micron , Microsoft , Nvidia and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. to purchase $26 billion of the company's Class N common stock in a private placement at a price per share equal to the IPO price. The shares sold in the private placement will not be registered in the offering and will not be subject to lock-up agreements with the underwriters, the company said.
As Anthropic executives get set to pitch the offering to investors, they have to contend with a tumultuous political environment , following last week's midterm elections that included a Democratic sweep in Congress and the passage of numerous statewide ballot measures that could slow the AI buildout. They're also facing a public market that's grown increasingly skeptical of the AI trade on concern that rising interest rates will make debt unaffordable for companies that need it for costly infrastructure purchases.
CNBC reported last week that some Anthropic investors were bracing for a lower valuation than had previously been expected. While Anthropic had been looking toward a $2 trillion valuation until recently, shareholders told CNBC that even $1.5 trillion is now in doubt, with one investor calling that number a "stretch."
Should Anthropic reach the Nasdaq this month as planned, under the ticker symbol "ANT," the debut would come roughly five months after SpaceX went public in a record offering that raised $85.7 billion. Elon Musk's reusable rocket and AI company has a market cap of just under $2 trillion, around its valuation at the time of the IPO.
Institutional demand for Anthropic is even stronger than it was for SpaceX at this point in the process, the people said. The company's book is already covered at the $70 to $78 per share range on an allocable basis, they said.
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei co-founded the AI lab in 2021 after he and a small group of researchers defected from OpenAI , now its chief rival. Anthropic is best known for developing a family of AI models called Claude, and the company primarily sells its products and services to other businesses.
On Monday, Anthropic introduced two new AI models, Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, the first time the company has released so-called frontier models since Amodei called to slow down the pace of AI development in September . Anthropic said that the models went through rigorous safety and alignment testing, and that the company developed new evaluations and post-launch monitoring tools ahead of the release.
For the nine months ended Sept. 30, Anthropic said it generated $33.24 billion in revenue up roughly 1,200% from the same period last year. It reported a $104 billion net loss during the nine-month period, though most of that was due to the change in fair value of convertible notes and derivative liabilities. Anthropic lost $25.1 billion over the same stretch in 2025, the filing said.
Anthropic said in its amended filing Tuesday that its run-rate revenue was roughly $81 billion at the end of October, up $10 billion from the previous month.
"Our aim is to help humankind chart a safe course through this technological evolution, open new frontiers of discovery, and bring forth an age of miracles," Anthropic's co-founders wrote in the prospectus. "Everyone who owns our stock, whether an institution or an individual, becomes part of that effort. We hope you will share our ambition to see it though."

articles.title_orig: Senate Banking Republican calls on Nvidia CEO to resign
articles.title_zh: Senate Banking Republican calls on Nvidia CEO to resign
articles.content_orig:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang walked into the chipmaker's Santa Clara, California, headquarters on Monday and conducted his regular morning meeting with top-level executives, people familiar with the meeting told CNBC.
On Sunday, Huang had disclosed an extramarital affair to employees .
Huang kicked off the closed-door gathering by addressing his infidelity and sharing how sorry he was to his staff, according to the people, who asked not to be named because they were not authorized to speak publicly. They said Huang didn't take any questions and quickly pivoted to business and top agenda items of the day.
The CEO was also in the office on Tuesday, conducting meetings just one week ahead of the company's quarterly earnings report.
Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
People inside the artificial intelligence chip giant said Huang tried to project "business as usual," even as the probe moved forward into his affair with an alleged Chinese spy. The CEO was in a romantic relationship with Alice Huang , a former Megaspeed executive, according to The Financial Times .
Sentiment toward Jensen Huang shifted on Sunday after the 63-year-old revealed in an email to employees that he had an affair, though he did not disclose with whom he had the relationship.
"I know an apology cannot undo what I have done," he wrote. "I hope our family will heal and that, over time, I can earn back your trust." Nvidia's board opened an investigation and hired Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct the probe on Tuesday.
Employees inside the firm described the mood to CNBC as "sad." One employee told CNBC that they were shocked by Jensen Huang's revelations.
People also told CNBC that longtime employees viewed Jensen Huang as an idol who could do no wrong and thought of him as a guiding light. Many employees at the company are also struggling to come to grips with the CEO's actions, the people said.
Jensen Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 to build graphics processing units for video game graphics. In recent years, the company has become synonymous with the AI boom, powering the technology that underpins large language models and the massive data center buildout.
A central figure in the development of every AI layer, the Nvidia CEO is also a key voice in Washington, even accompanying President Donald Trump on his trip to China in May . In September, Jensen Huang and his wife were pictured at the same table as Chinese President Xi Jinping for the White House's state dinner.
The news of the CEO's affair has drawn increased scrutiny on his continued support for more AI chip sales to China.

articles.title_zh: Stocks rally as CoreWeave soothes, bonds reel on rate hike fears
articles.content_orig:
Neocloud player CoreWeave saw shares swing in extended trading Tuesday afternoon after beating expectations on revenue in the third quarter .
The company also raised its guidance for the full year. Shares were initially positive in after hours before dipping into negative territory.
The results come as shares of CoreWeave have been subject to selling pressure amid rising worries that the artificial intelligence data center build-out could see a slowdown. The company's bond yields have also been marching higher.
Follow below as CNBC breaks down the biggest stock market moves of the day.
Mercury Systems , the maker of aerospace and defense electronics and signal and data processing systems fell almost 3% postmarket after rising 5% in regular trading Tuesday.
Mercury earned 52 cents a share in its fiscal first quarter, above the 33-cent highest estimate among 13 analysts polled by FactSet. Revenue of $253.2 million similarly beat the highest estimate on the Street, at $246.2 million.
Mercury shares are ahead 14.5% so far in 2026.
Grocery Outlet fell 8% after the company posted mixed results for the third quarter. The grocery store chain's revenue came in at $1.18 billion for the period, just above a FactSet consensus of $1.17 billion. Adjusted earnings per share totaled 16 cents, in line with estimates.
NextNav , the ground-based backup for GPS, climbed 8% postmarket after falling 6% during the regular trading session Tuesday.
Third-quarter revenue nearly doubled from the same period a year ago, while the quarterly loss narrowed to 4 cents a share from 12 cents last year. Cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments on hand rose to $264.1 million on Sept. 30 from $152.1 million on Dec. 31, the company said.
Based in Reston, Virginia, NextNav is down 50% in 2026 and has a market value of about $1.5 billion, according to FactSet data.
Shares climbed more than 9%.
CoreWeave shares traded 1% higher after the neocloud company reported third-quarter revenue that exceeded analyst expectations.
The company's top line came in at $3.66 billion, marking a 168% surge from the year-earlier period. Analysts polled by LSEG expected revenue of $3.55 billion. CoreWeave also hiked its full-year revenue outlook.
Rigetti Computing's third-quarter results disappointed the Street, sending shares down in after-hours trading.
The quantum computing stock was last down more than 6%.
Rigetti lost 8 cents per share, worse than the FactSet consensus estimate of a 5 cents per share loss. Revenue was well below expectations, landing at $1.4 million versus the consensus estimate of $3.5 million.
Full-year guidance also disappointed, with the company calling for roughly $20 million in revenue for the period, while the FactSet consensus sought $22.6 million.
The space company saw shares decline in extended trading after narrowing its full-year revenue guidance.
Firefly Aerospace sees revenue in a range of $440 million to $450 million, versus its earlier call for $420 million to $450 million. The FactSet consensus estimate sought $439.4 million.
Firefly's third-quarter report was better than expected, with the company reporting an adjusted loss of 45 cents a share on revenue of $110.7 million. Analysts polled by FactSet were looking for a loss of 50 cents a share and $102.3 million.
Microsoft shares dropped 3% in a sudden move after Anthropic announced a slate of new workplace tools for Claude that could compete with Office.
Anthropic introduced Claude Sheets, Claude Whiteboards and Claude Data in a blog post .
"Starting today, Claude can build spreadsheets, whiteboards, and dashboards with your team," the post said.
Shares of On Holding fell 8% as investors looked beyond a one-time tariff refund of 52.6 million Swiss francs and focused on a direct-to-consumer sales miss.
Adjusted earnings rose from a year earlier and topped the FactSet consensus estimate. Net income increased 36.9% to 162.8 million Swiss francs.
Net sales at the Swiss sportswear and athletic-footwear company rose 17.2% to 931.4 million Swiss francs, slightly above the FactSet consensus estimate of 930.3 million Swiss francs.
Broken down by segments, direct-to-consumer generated revenue of 393.3 million Swiss francs, falling short of the StreetAccount estimate for 417.7 million Swiss francs.
The company reported a gross margin of 72.6%, or 66.9% excluding the tariff refund.
Shares of the chip giant tumbled more than 6% on the day, touching $166.52 a share in midday trading.
Nvidia has been skidding to start the week as traders assess the fallout from CEO Jensen Huang's extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
Shares of Trump Media & Technology Group climbed 7% after the company reported a profitable third quarter and a surge in revenue over the period.
The company posted net income of $409.7 million in the third quarter, which includes gains on digital assets, up from the year-ago loss of $54.8 million. Revenue came in at $3 million, up more than 200% from the year-ago period.
Companies tied to home construction tumbled after October's consumer inflation report came in hot and market expectations for a December rate hike climbed.
Fed funds futures now suggests a 100% likelihood of a rate increase in December. Such a move would influence the bond market and in turn rates on mortgages.
The iShares U.S. Home Construction ETF (ITB) fell more than 3%.
Homebuilders Lennar and D.R. Horton lost 5% and 4%, respectively, while Floor & Decor Holdings slid 3%.
Carlyle Group fell 1% after UBS downgraded the stock to neutral from buy, cutting its price target to $47 from its prior target of $60.
Analyst Michael Brown sees the risk/reward as balanced, noting that Carlyle's newer growth businesses are not yet large enough to offset its dependence on flagship fundraising. Carlyle is increasingly likely to miss its 2028 earnings, according to the analyst.
"We lowered our fee-related earnings multiple to 8 times and price-to-earnings multiple to 8 times in our 50/50 blended SoTP framework," Brown said. "This reflects an estimated 10.7% three-year CAGR in fee-related earnings from 2025 to 2028, reduced visibility into when flagship funds will begin generating fees and a less diversified growth strategy than faster-growing peers."
Data center power producer GE Vernova is sliding in Tuesday morning trading following revisions from SoftBank on its power equipment procurement strategy. Shares of GEV are down close to 7% as of 10:35 a.m. ET.
Share of Steel Dynamics were up 4% after the company announced an additional $3 billion authorization for share repurchases. The authorization is effective immediately and is additive to the previous $1.5 billion program, which had $216 million remaining authorized and available for repurchase on Sept. 30, 2026.
The company's board of directors also declared a quarterly cash dividend of 53 cents per common share. The dividend is payable to shareholders of record at the close of business on Dec. 31, and is payable on or about Jan. 8, 2027.
"These actions reflect the Board's and senior leadership's continued confidence in our ability to consistently provide meaningful, industry-leading free cash flow generation throughout all market environments, in order to both continue our strong growth strategy and provide significant shareholder returns," stated Mark D. Millett, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer.
Chipmaker Nvidia is sagging for the second day in a row after CEO Jensen Huang issued an apology in the wake of a report that he was the target of a potential Chinese spying operation. Shares of the company were down 4% as of 9:45 a.m. in Tuesday trading. On Monday, shares also dropped 4%. Shares are down 25% over the past month amid broader struggles in the tech trade.
Shares of American Airlines were flat, outperforming the broader market after Rothschild upgraded the airline to buy from neutral.

articles.title_orig: Salvadoran troops target Haitian gang, leaving 20 dead
articles.title_zh: Salvadoran troops target Haitian gang, leaving 20 dead
articles.content_orig:
El Salvador’s President Nayib Bukele said that Salvadoran troops have targeted one of Haiti’s largest criminal organisations. It comes amid international calls to respect international human rights law.
Bukele announced the attack on Tuesday on the social media platform X.
“We destroyed the house of [gang leader] Lanmo San Jou and the 400 Mawozo gang’s headquarters,” the right-wing leader wrote.
Bukele posted a video of helicopters circling overhead and firing on the site in Croix-des-Bouquets, near Port-au-Prince.
The operation was reportedly conducted on Sunday by Haitian police with support from Salvadoran troops, and resulted in the killing of 20 people.
The announcement comes as Haiti’s prime minister, Alix Didier Fils-Aime, prepares to visit El Salvador next week to discuss the future of Salvadoran troops in his gang-plagued Caribbean nation.
Amnesty International has urged both countries to ensure that all operations conducted by Salvadoran forces in Haiti comply with international human rights law, and called on them to release the agreement governing the mass deployment.
“Both governments must make public the agreement governing the deployment and explain how they oversee the deployed forces, what rules govern the use of force, to whom they are accountable, and how people can report possible violations without fear of reprisals,” Amnesty’s Americas director Ana Piquer said.
“Ensure that all operations conducted by Salvadoran forces in Haiti comply with international human rights law,” she urged the leaders of the two nations.
She also called on both countries to establish “prompt, independent and impartial investigations into all allegations of human rights violations”.
“The response to gang violence must not replicate the abuses and impunity that have characterized previous interventions in Haiti,” she added.
Some 2,000 troops have been sent by El Salvador’s president to Haiti since the mid-October disappearance of four Salvadoran personnel.
The vast majority are not participating in the United Nations-backed Gang Suppression Force (GSF) , raising concerns about their rules of engagement.
Bukele initially stated the deployment aimed at bringing home four Salvadoran GSF soldiers who went missing during an ambush attack on October 18.
But more recently, he has hinted at a broader goal of eliminating Haiti’s powerful gangs, as he did in his own country with a campaign pockmarked with allegations of human rights abuses.
Haiti is set to hold elections in July and October next year, marking its first ones in more than a decade.

articles.title_orig: Anthropic opens Australian retail IPO offering as AI scrutiny intensifies
articles.title_zh: Anthropic opens Australian retail IPO offering as AI scrutiny intensifies
articles.content_orig:
Anthropic , the maker of AI chatbot Claude, opened its Australian retail initial public offering on Wednesday, giving individual investors access to shares ahead of the company's planned Nasdaq listing.
The offering opened at 10 a.m. Australian Eastern Daylight Time on Wednesday and is expected to close at 5 p.m. on Nov. 17, according to the timetable published by participating broker Stake.
Anthropic is seeking to raise as much as $64.4 billion in its IPO, with a separate $26 billion private placement, bringing a combined total to as much as $90.4 billion. Shares are expected to be priced between $70 to $78 each.
The Australian retail offering is expected to consist of newly issued Class A common shares under a prospectus to be lodged with the Australian Securities and Investments Commission, Anthropic said on its website .
Participating brokers include Commonwealth Bank of Australia's CommSec unit as lead broker, along with Bell Potter, LGT Wealth, Macquarie Group, Morgans, Morgan Stanley Wealth Management, Sharesies and Stake.
Anthropic said the prospectus would be available on its IPO website once the Australian retail offering opens. Investors will need to review the document and apply through participating brokers under the terms of the offer.
Australia is one of the small numbers of markets outside the U.S. where retail investors will be able to buy the company's shares directly, alongside Japan, Canada and parts of Europe.
The San Francisco-based AI startup has applied to list its Class A common stock on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol "ANT." Anthropic said it does not plan to seek a listing on the Australian Securities Exchange.
The offering comes as Australia moves to tighten oversight of AI companies after an OpenAI agent gained unauthorized access to the medical statistics website of Medicare,  the country's universal health insurance program.
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said Tuesday that the government would introduce mandatory reporting for certain AI-related incidents and establish an AI safety regulator with powers to enforce penalties.
"The law needs to get ahead of, and in some cases, make sure that it catches up with what is a very fast-changing world," Albanese told Reuters.
The government is also considering changes to criminal law for cases involving serious misconduct.
The country has also ruled out a copyright-law exemption that would allow AI companies to train models on Australian content without licensing it.
Open AI and Anthropic told Australian parliament last month that they would support mandatory reporting of data breaches involving their AI agents, acknowledging that disclosure is currently voluntary.

articles.title_orig: Anthropic bankers prepare to increase IPO valuation to $1.5tn or more
articles.title_zh: Anthropic bankers prepare to increase IPO valuation to $1.5tn or more
articles.content_orig:
Anthropic said it will offer 825 million shares in its upcoming IPO at a price range between $70 and $78 per share, according to an updated filing on Tuesday, bringing the 5-year-old artificial intelligence lab a step closer to a potentially historic Nasdaq debut.
The company is planning to price on Nov. 18 and trade on Nov. 19, according to people familiar with the details who were granted anonymity because they were not authorized to speak publicly. Anthropic is targeting retail allocation of about 20%, the people said, a much higher percentage than the typical initial public offering, which is 5% to 10% for retail investors.
At the high end of the range, Anthropic would net up to $64.35 billion in proceeds through the IPO. The company could end up being worth up to $1.405 trillion on a fully diluted basis, rising from the $965 billion valuation it announced as part of a funding round in May.
Anthropic said it has entered into an agreement with Advanced Micro Devices , Broadcom , Google , Micron , Microsoft , Nvidia and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. to purchase $26 billion of the company's Class N common stock in a private placement at a price per share equal to the IPO price. The shares sold in the private placement will not be registered in the offering and will not be subject to lock-up agreements with the underwriters, the company said.
As Anthropic executives get set to pitch the offering to investors, they have to contend with a tumultuous political environment , following last week's midterm elections that included a Democratic sweep in Congress and the passage of numerous statewide ballot measures that could slow the AI buildout. They're also facing a public market that's grown increasingly skeptical of the AI trade on concern that rising interest rates will make debt unaffordable for companies that need it for costly infrastructure purchases.
CNBC reported last week that some Anthropic investors were bracing for a lower valuation than had previously been expected. While Anthropic had been looking toward a $2 trillion valuation until recently, shareholders told CNBC that even $1.5 trillion is now in doubt, with one investor calling that number a "stretch."
Should Anthropic reach the Nasdaq this month as planned, under the ticker symbol "ANT," the debut would come roughly five months after SpaceX went public in a record offering that raised $85.7 billion. Elon Musk's reusable rocket and AI company has a market cap of just under $2 trillion, around its valuation at the time of the IPO.
Institutional demand for Anthropic is even stronger than it was for SpaceX at this point in the process, the people said. The company's book is already covered at the $70 to $78 per share range on an allocable basis, they said.
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei co-founded the AI lab in 2021 after he and a small group of researchers defected from OpenAI , now its chief rival. Anthropic is best known for developing a family of AI models called Claude, and the company primarily sells its products and services to other businesses.
On Monday, Anthropic introduced two new AI models, Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, the first time the company has released so-called frontier models since Amodei called to slow down the pace of AI development in September . Anthropic said that the models went through rigorous safety and alignment testing, and that the company developed new evaluations and post-launch monitoring tools ahead of the release.
For the nine months ended Sept. 30, Anthropic said it generated $33.24 billion in revenue up roughly 1,200% from the same period last year. It reported a $104 billion net loss during the nine-month period, though most of that was due to the change in fair value of convertible notes and derivative liabilities. Anthropic lost $25.1 billion over the same stretch in 2025, the filing said.
Anthropic said in its amended filing Tuesday that its run-rate revenue was roughly $81 billion at the end of October, up $10 billion from the previous month.
"Our aim is to help humankind chart a safe course through this technological evolution, open new frontiers of discovery, and bring forth an age of miracles," Anthropic's co-founders wrote in the prospectus. "Everyone who owns our stock, whether an institution or an individual, becomes part of that effort. We hope you will share our ambition to see it though."

articles.title_zh: Girl, 5, shoots and kills little sister, 3, after dad left loaded gun on kitchen counter
articles.content_orig:
A five-year-old girl fatally shot her little sister after their father reportedly left his loaded gun on the kitchen counter before he headed to bed.
Olivia Melo Moreira, 3, was found dead by her parents Sunday morning on the floor of their Rio de Janeiro home — as her stunned sister ran toward them repeatedly saying “Sorry, Daddy,” the devastated father told police, according to The Sun .
Moreira was rushed to a local hospital where she succumbed to her injuries, O Globo reported .
The dad, a licensed gun owner who has not yet been identified, was interviewed by police.
He was not immediately arrested but is expected to be charged with involuntary manslaughter and failure to exercise proper caution with a firearm, according to The Sun.
“At this very delicate and tragic moment, the family has no interest whatsoever in making a statement,” the dad’s attorney told reporters.
The little girl’s family had been out late for a street party that went on until 6 a.m. Sunday morning. When they returned to the house, Moreira’s mother noticed the garage gate was wide open and alerted her husband, who took his pistol downstairs to check whether anyone had broken in.
He found no burglars and went back to bed — but tragically left the loaded pistol, still in its holster, on the kitchen counter.
A loud bang awoke the parents who discovered their daughter on the floor.
Morning Report delivers the latest news, videos, photos and more.
The father had registered the weapon as a licensed sports shooter and hunter.
Police have seized the gun and the investigation remains ongoing.

By XANTHA LEATHAM, EXECUTIVE SCIENCE EDITOR
Published: 05:34 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 05:34 EST, 10 November 2026
Scientists aboard China 's Tiangong space station have chilled a cloud of atoms to just 9.7 picokelvin, the coldest temperature ever measured.
The record-breaking experiment took advantage of the station's microgravity environment, allowing researchers to study matter at temperatures closer to absolute zero than ever before.
The atoms were chilled to just 9.7 trillionths of a degree above absolute zero, around 280 billion times colder than the average temperature of the Universe.
The feat smashes the previous record of 38 picokelvin, which was achieved in a microgravity experiment on Earth in 2021.
Researchers say the breakthrough opens a new frontier in the quest to understand the strangest laws of quantum physics.
‘This record-low temperature could stimulate a new generation of…experiments in quantum simulation and precision measurements in space,’ the team, from Peking University and the Chinese Academy of Sciences, wrote in the journal Science .
The experiment was carried out using the Cold Atom Physics Rack housed inside the Mengtian laboratory module of China's orbiting space station
Researchers calculated the record-breaking temperature by tracking the slow expansion of an ultracold cloud of atoms, which remained visible for seven seconds after being released
The experiment was carried out using the Cold Atom Physics Rack housed inside the Mengtian laboratory module of China's orbiting space station.
The weightless environment of space was crucial because gravity on Earth makes it harder to keep ultracold atoms stable for long periods.
Inside the facility, scientists trapped about 20,000 rubidium atoms and cooled them until they formed an exotic state of matter known as a Bose-Einstein condensate.
This bizarre state occurs when atoms become so cold that they begin behaving like a single giant quantum object.
To push temperatures even lower, the team transferred the atoms into a trap made of laser light and allowed them to expand under carefully controlled conditions.
The researchers were able to observe the freezing cloud of atoms for an extraordinary seven seconds as it expanded freely.
Inside the facility, scientists trapped about 20,000 rubidium atoms and cooled them until they formed an exotic state of matter known as a Bose-Einstein condensate
This image illustrates atoms held in an optical trap aboard China's space station, where they were cooled to 10 picokelvin - the lowest temperature reached in space
While the temperatures involved are almost impossible to comprehend, they are still technically above absolute zero, the theoretical point at which all atomic motion ceases.
Scientists have pursued ever-lower temperatures for decades because ultracold atoms provide an ideal laboratory for testing fundamental physics.
Experiments at these temperatures could help researchers probe mysterious quantum states that cannot be studied under ordinary conditions.
The work may also pave the way for a new generation of ultra-sensitive atom interferometers capable of making exquisitely precise measurements.
Such instruments could one day be used to test Einstein's theory of gravity, hunt for new physics and even aid future gravitational-wave detection efforts.
The researchers say their all-optical cooling platform is particularly well suited to future space missions because it can be adapted for a wide range of experiments.

articles.title_orig: SpaceX plans $24 billion data center project in Starbase
articles.title_zh: SpaceX plans $24 billion data center project in Starbase
articles.content_orig:

McALLEN — SpaceX is planning to build a $24 billion data center and power plant just outside of Brownsville on property that the city had just de-annexed earlier this year at the company’s request, circumventing Brownsville’s data center moratorium that went into effect last week.
On Monday, the city of Starbase, which later annexed land where the project will be built into their city limits, notified the public that SpaceX is building a $24 billion “gas-fired power plant and super-compute facility.”
The $24 billion investment is expected to cover the initial phases of the project which could include future expansions, according to the Monday notice which stated that the Starbase city commissioners are scheduled to hold a public hearing in December in which they will consider tax breaks for the project.
The 444.45 acres of land where the project will be located was the subject of local scrutiny over the summer, when SpaceX asked the city of Brownsville to de-annex that land. In exchange, the company offered to fund $220 million for city water and wastewater projects.
A SpaceX representative didn’t provide details as to why the company wanted the land, located near the Port of Brownsville out of Brownsville’s city limits, but the company pressured the city to approve the de-annexation quickly or else the $220 million would be off the table. The city agreed, but the move drew widespread condemnation from residents and environmental activists who believed the city was allowing SpaceX to further take over land in the area.
Soon after the city approved the deal, speculation circulated online that SpaceX planned to build a data center on the property and wished to circumvent a data center moratorium that was advancing within Brownsville.
That speculation appears to have been correct all along.
In response to the news, the South Texas Environmental Justice Network, announced a protest against the project, arguing that the new facilities would pollute the air, use up water and increase energy bills for residents.
Other residents responded positively, seeing the project as a source for more jobs.
“There’s a lot of people that need jobs in our community and SpaceX has contributed to those jobs,” said Janie Melendez, a Brownsville resident and school teacher.
She previously served on the Texas Republican Party’s executive committee but said her politics don’t influence her view on data centers and SpaceX.
“Since SpaceX moved in, my home has tripled in value,” she said. “But I’m one of those [people] that tries to find a balance in everything.”
SpaceX did not respond to questions regarding the project.
However, a majority of Texans oppose data center construction, which has received a wave of pushback across the state due to concerns over how much power and water they require to operate at a time when utility bills remain high and water scarcity fears mount. In response to public backlash, several communities have issued temporary moratoriums on data centers.
As criticisms of these facilities grew, Gov. Greg Abbott directed operators of the electric grid in August to pause requests for data center connections to the grid until the data centers could be audited. However, not all data centers rely on the state’s power grid and therefore could still move forward by supplying their own electricity.
The gas-fired power plant that SpaceX plans to build could provide power to its data center to avoid connecting to the state’s power grid.
Abbott also ordered the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality to stop issuing permits for data centers, though critics say that some permits have continued to advance through the permitting process.
Data center developers could face stronger headwinds under Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa , who said she would issue a ban on all data center approvals until state legislators can pass laws “to protect Texans,” she said in a video posted on X .
Brownsville approved its own 90-day moratorium which went into effect last week, temporarily hitting pause on data center applications within the city and its extraterritorial jurisdiction. Had the 444.45-acre tract of land remained within Brownsville’s city limits, the SpaceX project likely would have had to find a different location.
The city of Brownsville said it stood by its decision to de-annex the property, which was based on “information and circumstances presented at the time,” the city said in a statement. That included the property’s location, municipal service considerations and potential long-term benefits to Brownsville.
The city further noted that the land was privately owned and its sale to SpaceX was a transaction between private parties.
The $220 million that the city received for the de-annexation will fund critical water infrastructure which the city said would help ensure their water supply keeps up with their future growth.
“The City recognizes the concerns raised about data center development and takes those concerns seriously,” the city said. “It remains committed to evaluating those concerns and protecting water resources, evaluating infrastructure impacts and ensuring responsible growth that serves Brownsville’s long-term interests.”
Further, the city assured that any future de-annexation requests will be evaluated independently under state law and the city commission will take the circumstances and legal requirements into consideration before taking action.
“Residents should have confidence that their concerns about data center development, water resources, energy consumption and responsible growth are being taken seriously,” the city said. “Our responsibility is to ensure that Brownsville’s growth is intentional, that residents’ interests remain a priority, and that decisions involving our community’s future are made with transparency, accountability and careful consideration.”

articles.title_orig: Ukraine's Zelenskiy says he is pleased with messages from US envoys on diplomatic efforts to end war
articles.title_zh: Ukraine's Zelenskiy says he is pleased with messages from US envoys on diplomatic efforts to end war
articles.content_orig:
In brief: President Volodymyr Zelensky said Russian military and intelligence officials presented false battlefield claims during Abu Dhabi peace talks. He challenged Moscow’s territorial demands, called for greater US pressure on Russia, and expressed readiness for direct negotiations with Putin.
President Volodymyr Zelensky said Tuesday, Nov. 10, that Russian negotiators had made false claims about controlling Ukrainian-held territory in Donbas, warning that Russian President Vladimir Putin appeared to be operating in a different reality as Washington attempts to broker an end to the war.
Speaking at a press conference in Copenhagen following meetings with Nordic leaders, Zelensky said Russian military and intelligence representatives claimed to control roughly half of the Donbas territory that remains under Ukrainian control.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
According to Zelensky, Ukrainian negotiators were stunned by the assertions and challenged the Russian delegation with video and photographic evidence.
“It’s not like, you know, one village,” Zelensky said, emphasizing that the disputed claims concerned a substantial area.
He said Russian representatives had seriously defended their version of the battlefield situation, despite evidence presented by Ukraine.
“I think that Putin lives a little bit in another different information. It’s [a] different reality,” Zelensky said.
The president suggested Putin was also telling American negotiators that Russia could seize the remaining eastern territories of Ukraine within months.
“Look, I need one, two, three months, and we will occupy the eastern part totally of Ukraine,” Zelensky said, describing what he believed Putin was communicating to Washington.
“But it’s not true. It’s not reality.”
Zelensky said American representatives had confirmed Ukraine’s assessment of the battlefield situation, which he described as an important development in the negotiations.
Despite the disagreements, Zelensky said he was prepared to discuss territorial questions directly with Putin, with mediation from the US and Europe.
“That’s why we are ready to sit and speak about territory,” he said.
He argued that such negotiations should take place at the level of national leaders because they require a clear understanding of actual territorial control.
“I know everything, and I think that the leader of Russia has to know everything, where we are,” Zelensky said.
Rejecting Moscow’s demands for Ukrainian withdrawals, he added:
“He said that you have to leave from here. I don’t understand why, because it’s our land.”
Zelensky also cited Kherson, divided by the Dnipro River, as an example of the complexity of territorial negotiations.
“On one bank there are Russians, on another bank we control everything. But people want to live [on] both banks, and this is a Ukrainian city,” he said.
“Such questions are sensitive. Yes, they are very difficult, but we have to speak about it.”
Zelensky said Ukraine would raise the possibility of a meeting between leaders during the next round of negotiations on Wednesday, Nov. 11.
“I’m not sure that Russia is ready, but we will raise this topic.”
Zelensky also questioned Washington’s approach to Russia, arguing that expanding commercial engagement or potentially lifting sanctions would be less effective than increasing economic pressure on Moscow.
“We don’t trust, but we hope. We can’t live without hope,” Zelensky said when asked whether the latest negotiations could produce better results than previous rounds.
He stressed that Ukraine supports diplomacy but believes Russia still faces insufficient pressure.
“We need more pressure on Russia, it’s true,” he said.
“I think that we need more pressure, less business with these guys, and it will be more useful.”
Zelensky nevertheless defended the decision to resume negotiations, saying that even a prisoner exchange would represent meaningful progress.
“Even if the result will be exchange, it’s a success. People will go home,” Zelensky said.
Zelensky also expressed concern about discussions between Washington and Moscow on a new European security architecture, warning that the initiative could revive demands Putin presented to then-US President Joe Biden in 2021.
He said Ukraine and its Nordic allies remained cautious because the details of the American-Russian discussions had not been shared.
“Nobody really understands 100% what they want,” Zelensky said.
“Nobody saw the documents, what they discussed, I mean Americans with Russians.”
He suggested the current proposals resembled Putin’s earlier attempts to reshape Europe’s security order.
“To my mind, and I stay on my version, that this is the same idea what Putin tried to raise with President Biden in 2021 about changing architecture,” he said.
Zelensky insisted that negotiations must follow a clear sequence: first end Russia’s war against Ukraine, then establish security guarantees for Kyiv, and only afterward consider broader European security arrangements.
“This sequence is very, very important,” he said.
He also expressed hope that the US Congress would take a more decisive role in supporting Ukraine, particularly in securing long-term American security guarantees.
Asked whether he could forgive Putin and how Ukrainians and Russians might eventually reconcile, Zelensky rejected the idea that reconciliation could substitute for justice.
“No, of course not,” he said when asked about forgiveness.
“They killed not abstract, [but] a very concrete number of people in very concrete cities, and they made a lot of tragedies with concrete lives… I’m just a human. I’m not God.”
He insisted that those responsible for killings and other atrocities must be identified and held accountable through legal proceedings.
“They have to answer,” he said, adding that courts and judges must determine responsibility.
“We didn’t begin this war,” Zelensky said, stressing that Ukraine’s demand remains unchanged: Russia must end its aggression, stop the war and pursue a diplomatic resolution.

articles.title_orig: House Republicans consider issuing subpoena to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang - ABC News
articles.title_zh: House Republicans consider issuing subpoena to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang - ABC News
articles.source: Breaking News, Latest News and Videos
articles.content_orig:
Several House Republicans called for a closed-door briefing.
The Republican chair of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, Rep. Brian Mast, told ABC News on Tuesday that he's prepared to subpoena Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang if he does not respond by Wednesday to a request from several House Republicans for a closed-door briefing on Huang's reported relationship with an alleged Chinese spy.
Last week, Mast as well as Rick Crawford, the chair of the House Intelligence Committee, and John Moolenaar, the chair of the House China Committee, sent Huang a letter requesting he appear for a "joint, closed-door briefing."
The focus of the briefing would be on Nvidia's "security protocols against foreign adversary espionage" after the tech giant on Sunday announced an investigation into its CEO following New York Times' reporting that he had an affair with an alleged Chinese government agent, identified as Alice Huang, a top executive at Singapore-based data company Megaspeed.
Jensen Huang has not yet responded to the Republicans' request that he appear for a briefing. Asked by ABC News if he would consider issuing a subpoena to Huang should he not respond, Mast said "absolutely."
It's unclear how a potential subpoena of Huang would play out. House Republicans lose control of their committees in January when the chamber turns over to Democrats. The subpoena would likely expire and Democrats would need to issue a new one.
ABC News reached out to Nvidia for comment from Huang for this story.
Congressional Republicans on the Select Committee on China also sent a letter to Huang requesting that he appear for a closed-door briefing Nov. 18 concerning his relationship with Alice Huang. It is not known if Huang will appear before that committee; Nvidia hasn't publicly responded to the request.
Mast said there is a "lengthy" list of things he wants to hear from the Nvidia CEO including what correspondence he had with the Chinese government. Mast added that he is "100%" worried about the national security implications of Huang's reported relationship given that he runs the world's largest computer chip manufacturer.
"They're American chips. You know. So we thank God that Jensen is an American entrepreneur. You know, it's an American tech company because they're the best chips anywhere in the globe," Mast said. "But that being said, we don't want China to access them, to use them, to produce them like that."
Nvidia's board said they have "no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised" by Huang's affair.
Huang "fully supports the review" and will cooperate with it, the Nvidia statement further said.
Several Democrats have expressed concerns about national security after the report, with House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries telling ABC News that there are "real concerns" that need to be addressed.
"We're going to need a full briefing, specifically as it relates to the Nvidia issue, so we can all get to the bottom of what has happened and what the implications are in terms of America's national security," Jeffries said.
On Monday, President Donald Trump said the FBI is investigating the matter. Trump said he spoke with Huang in a phone call on Monday, during which the CEO said that he "didn't know" he was involved with an alleged Chinese spy.
"He said he had absolutely no idea that the person in question was a spy," the president told reporters during a press briefing on Monday.
It's unclear when -- if ever -- the Trump administration alerted Nvidia that its CEO was the target of an alleged Chinese espionage plot.
The Chinese government has denied the allegations, calling them "baseless and purely slanderous smears against China."
Neither Alice Huang nor her employer, Megaspeed International, responded to ABC News' request for comment about the New York Times story on the relationship.

articles.title_orig: Stanley Zabar Has Died. He Managed the Books, and the Slaw, at a N.Y.C. Landmark.
articles.title_zh: Stanley Zabar Has Died. He Managed the Books, and the Slaw, at a N.Y.C. Landmark.
articles.content_orig:
NEW YORK CITY (WABC) -- Stanley Zabar, the co-owner of the iconic Upper West Side gourmet grocery store Zabar's, has died at the age of 94, according to a statement posted on the store's Instagram page .
The statement described Zabar as a "quiet force behind our family business," with Stanley having "spent decades working with his brother Saul to build upon and carry forward the vision of their parents, Louis and Lillian Zabar."
Zabar's legal and financial acumen was described as "vital" in shaping the Zabar's into a beloved New York City institution, that was first founded by his parents in 1934.
The Upper West Side shop is known for its fancy cheese, smoked fish, and coffee among other specialty items.
Over time, five locations were consolidated into a large single market at West 80th and Broadway.
Stanley's death comes just over a year after his older brother Saul died at the age of 97.

articles.title_orig: Mojtaba Khamenei aide's chilling '40 years' warning surfaces amid US push for Iran deal
articles.title_zh: Mojtaba Khamenei aide's chilling '40 years' warning surfaces amid US push for Iran deal
articles.content_orig:
Fox News senior strategic analyst Ret. Gen. Jack Keane discusses reports that Vice President JD Vance contacted an Iranian hard-liner at President Donald Trump’s direction. Keane argues that Iran is not serious about reaching a deal and would not comply with one.
Iran's top security official, who reportedly received a letter from Vice President JD Vance about resuming peace talks, warned in a resurfaced interview that wartime negotiations with Tehran could drag on for decades, and during which both sides should "be prepared to fight."
Mohsen Rezaei, a former commander of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), now serves as secretary of the Supreme National Security Council and acts as a key aide to Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei. He also helped shape Tehran's military strategy during the 1980-88 Iran-Iraq War .
That eight-year conflict ended after Iran's then-supreme leader, Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini, accepted a U.N.-brokered cease-fire that he famously likened to drinking from a "poisoned chalice."
JD VANCE RETURNS TO WASHINGTON AFTER 16 HOURS OF IRAN PEACE TALKS COLLAPSE IN PAKISTAN
Senior Iranian general Mohsen Rezaei issues a direct threat against President Donald Trump as the U.S. repositions aircraft carrier amid rising tensions with Tehran, according to reports. (Ayoub Ghaderi/YJC/WANA (West Asia News Agency) via REUTERS)
"Ceasefire means an unfinished war," Rezaei had said of the war in a 2006 interview with the Iranian publication Baztab. An English translation of the interview is preserved by George Washington University's National Security Archive .
Asked whether both sides would remain in their positions and begin talks, Rezaei replied: "Yes. Negotiations can take 30 to 40 years and during that time Iran and Iraq should be prepared to fight."
Two decades after suggesting negotiations could drag on for years, Washington has reportedly been seeking talks with Rezaei, a key power player in Iran’s current military leadership.
Vance sent him a letter proposing renewed peace talks between the United States and Iran in October, the Wall Street Journal reported.
Iran said it had received a letter from Vance but had not responded, according to Iranian state media. The semi-official Tasnim News Agency said Iran was awaiting U.S. compliance with its conditions, warning that "any position that contradicts this framework is unacceptable."
TRUMP SAYS IRAN DEAL ‘LARGELY NEGOTIATED’ AS 84-DAY WAR NEARS POSSIBLE END
In June, President Donald Trump had posted a warning on Truth Social that Iran had taken too long to come to terms and would "pay the price," while on Monday, he also said that Iran wanted a deal but warned that another U.S. strike could be about five times as large as the previous.
"We could knock it out fast, or we could knock it out over a short, not a long period of time," Trump said during a C-SPAN interview on " Washington Journal Primetime ."
"I can tell you that Iran would like to make a deal, and we'll find out whether that'll happen," Trump said of the current timeframe.
Rezaei however, has continued to maintain a defiant stance toward Washington, writing on X on Nov. 9: "The war on Iran has already wrecked the US government," he wrote before adding that "Washington flails like a desperate gambler."
"FOLD YOUR HAND. STOP manufacturing FAKE NEWS about imaginary talks.
"Stop denying the West Asian NEW ORDER. Time to SURRENDER to the seven conditions Iran has repeatedly set out," he said.
Following the Nov. 3 U.S. midterm elections, Rezaei also claimed Iran had defeated Washington militarily and politically.
He warned of a "devastating response" to another attack and declared it was time for Washington to "SURRENDER."
RUBIO DEFENDS TRUMP'S IRAN WAR AS NOT 'NECESSARILY POPULAR, BUT NECESSARY'
Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) generals and commanders, Mohsen Rezaei (2nd L), Ali Fadavi (3rd L), Ahmad Vahidi (2nd R), and Hassan Hassanzadeh (R) attend a memorial ceremony for IRGC commanders, nuclear scientists, and civilians killed in the Iran-Israel war at the Imam Khomeini Grand Mosque in downtown Tehran, Iran, on July 2, 2025. (Morteza Nikoubazl/NurPhoto via Getty Images)
Rezaei also rejected reports of ongoing U.S.-Iran negotiations or any planned meeting in Qatar , accusing Washington of spreading false claims to ease economic pressure and lower oil prices. He reiterated that Tehran would not reopen the Strait of Hormuz until its seven conditions were met.
Rezaei has spent more than four decades in Iran's defense establishment. He commanded the IRGC from 1981 to 1997, overseeing operations during the Iran-Iraq War.
In the 2006 Baztab interview, Rezaei also detailed how Iranian leaders distinguished their public rhetoric from military strategy.
Although Khomeini and other Iranian officials called for "fighting till Saddam is toppled" and "until the nuisance is eradicated," Rezaei said Tehran's actual strategy was "fighting up to a victory."
At the time, Iran's battlefield gains, he suggested, were meant to strengthen Tehran's negotiating position rather than achieve total conquest.
IRAN VOWS ‘ASTONISHING’ STRIKES AND LIFTS MISSILE-RANGE LIMIT AS US TARGETS LAND ROUTES
Commanders and members of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps meet with Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in Tehran, Iran, on Aug. 17, 2023. (Office of the Iranian Supreme Leader/WANA (West Asia News Agency)/Reuters)
"The world did not pay attention to the slogans," Rezaei said in the interview, adding that foreign governments and intelligence agencies focused on Iranian leaders' actions and diplomatic positions.
Rezaei also said Iran had struggled to turn battlefield gains into diplomatic victories because it lacked international alliances and influence at the United Nations.
Rezaei has since faced U.S. sanctions and international scrutiny. The Trump administration first sanctioned him Jan. 10, 2020, under an executive order targeting senior Iranian officials appointed by the supreme leader.
Rezaei had also been accused of involvement in the July 1994 bombing of the Argentine Israelite Mutual Association Jewish community center in Buenos Aires, which killed 85 people.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Interpol approved an Argentine request for a Red Notice against Rezaei in 2007 in connection with the bombing.
Emma Bussey is a breaking news writer for Fox News Digital. Before joining Fox, she worked at The Telegraph with the U.S. overnight team, across desks including foreign, politics, news, sport and culture.
